# diceR

## Overview

The goal of `diceR` is to provide a systematic framework for generating
diverse cluster ensembles in R. There are a lot of nuances in cluster
analysis to consider. We provide a process and a suite of functions and
tools to implement a systematic framework for cluster discovery, guiding
the user through the generation of a diverse clustering solutions from
data, ensemble formation, algorithm selection and the arrival at a final
consensus solution. We have additionally developed visual and analytical
validation tools to help with the assessment of the final result. We
implemented a wrapper function
[`dice()`](https://alinetalhouk.github.io/diceR/reference/dice.md) that
allows the user to easily obtain results and assess them. Thus, the
package is accessible to both end user with limited statistical
knowledge. Full access to the package is available for informaticians
and statisticians and the functions are easily expanded. More details
can be found in our companion paper published at [BMC
Bioinformatics](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12859-017-1996-y).

## Installation

You can install `diceR` from CRAN with:

``` r

install.packages("diceR")
```

Or get the latest development version from GitHub:

``` r

# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("AlineTalhouk/diceR")
```

## Example

The following example shows how to use the main function of the package,
[`dice()`](https://alinetalhouk.github.io/diceR/reference/dice.md). A
data matrix `hgsc` contains a subset of gene expression measurements of
High Grade Serous Carcinoma Ovarian cancer patients from the Cancer
Genome Atlas publicly available datasets. Samples as rows, features as
columns. The function below runs the package through the
[`dice()`](https://alinetalhouk.github.io/diceR/reference/dice.md)
function. We specify (a range of) `nk` clusters over `reps` subsamples
of the data containing 80% of the full samples. We also specify the
clustering `algorithms` to be used and the ensemble functions used to
aggregated them in `cons.funs`.

``` r

library(diceR)
data(hgsc)
obj <- dice(
  hgsc,
  nk = 4,
  reps = 5,
  algorithms = c("hc", "diana"),
  cons.funs = c("kmodes", "majority"),
  progress = FALSE,
  verbose = FALSE
)
```

The first few cluster assignments are shown below:

``` r

knitr::kable(head(obj$clusters))
```

|                     | kmodes | majority |
|:--------------------|-------:|---------:|
| TCGA.04.1331_PRO.C5 |      2 |        2 |
| TCGA.04.1332_MES.C1 |      2 |        2 |
| TCGA.04.1336_DIF.C4 |      4 |        2 |
| TCGA.04.1337_MES.C1 |      2 |        2 |
| TCGA.04.1338_MES.C1 |      2 |        2 |
| TCGA.04.1341_PRO.C5 |      2 |        2 |

You can also compare the base `algorithms` with the `cons.funs` using
internal evaluation indices:

``` r

knitr::kable(obj$indices$ii$`4`)
```

|  | Algorithms | calinski_harabasz | dunn | pbm | tau | gamma | c_index | davies_bouldin | mcclain_rao | sd_dis | ray_turi | g_plus | silhouette | s_dbw | Compactness | Connectivity |
|:---|:---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| HC_Euclidean | HC_Euclidean | 3.104106 | 0.2608547 | 59.73711 | 0 | 0.4285714 | 0.2844073 | 1.839182 | 0.8009149 | 0.1306062 | 1.4765665 | 0 | NaN | NaN | 24.83225 | 41.62183 |
| DIANA_Euclidean | DIANA_Euclidean | 53.647400 | 0.3348103 | 33.87817 | 0 | -1.8750000 | 0.1589442 | 2.824201 | 0.8051915 | 0.2119281 | 3.2978986 | 0 | 0.0692233 | NaN | 21.93396 | 241.66310 |
| kmodes | kmodes | 55.138600 | 0.3396909 | 50.51722 | 0 | -0.6822430 | 0.1453599 | 2.006752 | 0.7972999 | 0.1170829 | 1.1408258 | 0 | 0.1253664 | NaN | 21.91494 | 201.42540 |
| majority | majority | 19.373248 | 0.3544371 | 85.05173 | 0 | -1.1651376 | 0.2102487 | 1.622799 | 0.8019453 | 0.1108674 | 0.9200511 | 0 | 0.1884934 | NaN | 23.85408 | 64.04921 |

## Pipeline

This figure is a visual schematic of the pipeline that
[`dice()`](https://alinetalhouk.github.io/diceR/reference/dice.md)
implements.

![Ensemble Clustering pipeline.](reference/figures/pipeline.png)

Ensemble Clustering pipeline.

Please visit the
[overview](https://alinetalhouk.github.io/diceR/articles/overview.html "diceR overview")
page for more detail.

# Package index

## Functions

- [`consensus_cluster()`](https://alinetalhouk.github.io/diceR/reference/consensus_cluster.md)
  : Consensus clustering
- [`consensus_combine()`](https://alinetalhouk.github.io/diceR/reference/consensus_combine.md)
  : Combine algorithms
- [`consensus_evaluate()`](https://alinetalhouk.github.io/diceR/reference/consensus_evaluate.md)
  : Evaluate, trim, and reweigh algorithms
- [`consensus_matrix()`](https://alinetalhouk.github.io/diceR/reference/consensus_matrix.md)
  : Consensus matrix
- [`graph_cdf()`](https://alinetalhouk.github.io/diceR/reference/graphs.md)
  [`graph_delta_area()`](https://alinetalhouk.github.io/diceR/reference/graphs.md)
  [`graph_heatmap()`](https://alinetalhouk.github.io/diceR/reference/graphs.md)
  [`graph_tracking()`](https://alinetalhouk.github.io/diceR/reference/graphs.md)
  [`graph_all()`](https://alinetalhouk.github.io/diceR/reference/graphs.md)
  : Graphical Displays
- [`ev_nmi()`](https://alinetalhouk.github.io/diceR/reference/external_validity.md)
  [`ev_confmat()`](https://alinetalhouk.github.io/diceR/reference/external_validity.md)
  : External validity indices
- [`impute_knn()`](https://alinetalhouk.github.io/diceR/reference/impute_knn.md)
  : K-Nearest Neighbours imputation
- [`impute_missing()`](https://alinetalhouk.github.io/diceR/reference/impute_missing.md)
  : Impute missing values
- [`pcn_simulate()`](https://alinetalhouk.github.io/diceR/reference/pcn.md)
  [`pcn_select()`](https://alinetalhouk.github.io/diceR/reference/pcn.md)
  : Simulate and select null distributions on empirical gene-gene
  correlations
- [`dice()`](https://alinetalhouk.github.io/diceR/reference/dice.md) :
  Diverse Clustering Ensemble
- [`CSPA()`](https://alinetalhouk.github.io/diceR/reference/CSPA.md) :
  Cluster-based Similarity Partitioning Algorithm (CSPA)
- [`k_modes()`](https://alinetalhouk.github.io/diceR/reference/k_modes.md)
  : K-modes
- [`majority_voting()`](https://alinetalhouk.github.io/diceR/reference/majority_voting.md)
  : Majority voting
- [`LCE()`](https://alinetalhouk.github.io/diceR/reference/LCE.md) :
  Linkage Clustering Ensemble
- [`LCA()`](https://alinetalhouk.github.io/diceR/reference/LCA.md) :
  Latent Class Analysis
- [`PAC()`](https://alinetalhouk.github.io/diceR/reference/PAC.md) :
  Proportion of Ambiguous Clustering
- [`cts()`](https://alinetalhouk.github.io/diceR/reference/similarity.md)
  [`srs()`](https://alinetalhouk.github.io/diceR/reference/similarity.md)
  [`asrs()`](https://alinetalhouk.github.io/diceR/reference/similarity.md)
  : Similarity Matrices
- [`compactness()`](https://alinetalhouk.github.io/diceR/reference/compactness.md)
  : Compactness Measure
- [`prepare_data()`](https://alinetalhouk.github.io/diceR/reference/prepare_data.md)
  : Prepare data for consensus clustering
- [`relabel_class()`](https://alinetalhouk.github.io/diceR/reference/relabel_class.md)
  : Relabel classes to a standard
- [`min_fnorm()`](https://alinetalhouk.github.io/diceR/reference/min_fnorm.md)
  : Minimize Frobenius norm for between two matrices
- [`sigclust()`](https://alinetalhouk.github.io/diceR/reference/sigclust.md)
  : Significant Testing of Clustering Results

## Data

- [`hgsc`](https://alinetalhouk.github.io/diceR/reference/hgsc.md) :
  Gene expression data for High Grade Serous Carcinoma from TCGA
